# PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness

# PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-27 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] CBT-I is a preferred behavioral approach to insomnia, but PD-specific efficacy and implementation should be described cautiously: the computerized ACCORD-PD trial showed better insomnia scores among completers, yet its intention-to-treat comparison was not significant and treatment dropout was high. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/

## How it works

- [statement] Polysomnography is not routine for uncomplicated insomnia assessment, but can help when sleep-disordered breathing, RBD or other sleep-related movements may explain disturbed sleep. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/
- [statement] NICE recommends considering modafinil for PD-related excessive daytime sleepiness only after a detailed sleep history excludes reversible drug-related and physical causes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] The cited review describes insomnia assessment as including a clinical sleep interview that checks medication effects, the sleep environment and comorbid sleep disorders; it notes that polysomnography is not routine for insomnia but may help when sleep-disordered breathing, RBD or other nocturnal movements are suspected. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/
- [statement] NICE advises that PD patients with daytime sleepiness or sudden sleep onset avoid driving and consider occupational hazards, with specialist-guided medication adjustment. It advises considering modafinil only after a detailed sleep history excludes reversible medication-related and physical causes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The ACCORD-PD pilot found greater insomnia improvement among computerized CBT-I completers than education completers, but not in intention-to-treat analysis; dropout in the CBT-I group was 43%. Adherence limits generalizability. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PD sleep complaints require separate assessment of insomnia, REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and excessive daytime sleepiness; results on overall sleep quality should not be assumed to establish efficacy for each phenotype. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13612690/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/
- [statement] The September 2026 phenotype-stratified meta-analysis concluded that pharmacological evidence for PD daytime sleepiness, insomnia and RBD remained insufficient for definitive recommendations; very high heterogeneity made pooled estimates for those domains exploratory. Improvement in overall sleep quality must not be substituted for proof of a specific sleep-disorder benefit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13612690/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] NICE recommends considering clonazepam or melatonin for PD-related RBD after reviewing medication causes; the 2023 AASM guideline conditionally suggests clonazepam and specifically immediate-release melatonin for secondary RBD. These are conditional treatment options rather than proof that every formulation works. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] In a placebo-controlled trial of thirty people with PD-RBD, prolonged-release melatonin 4 mg did not reduce RBD events; the primary endpoint comparison was not significant (P = 0.92). This finding concerns that formulation and trial, rather than disproving all melatonin regimens. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674060/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] A negative prolonged-release melatonin trial should not be presented as a test of immediate-release melatonin: in 30 PD patients, 4 mg prolonged-release melatonin over 8 weeks did not reduce RBD compared with placebo, while AASM separately conditionally recommends immediate-release melatonin and finds insufficient evidence for prolonged-release melatonin in secondary RBD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7027846/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] In the ACCORD-PD pilot, 28 participants were recruited; completion was 8/14 with computerized CBT-I versus 13/14 with standard education. Insomnia Severity Index improvement favored CBT-I among completers (−7.9 versus −3.5), but the intention-to-treat comparison was not significant (p = 0.48). (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/
- [statement] Modafinil is a conditional clinical option rather than a reliably effective treatment for every sleepy PD patient: NICE says to consider it after excluding reversible causes, but a placebo-controlled trial of 40 patients found no significant improvement in subjective Epworth sleepiness or objective multiple sleep latency testing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1739456/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] RBD involves loss of REM muscle atonia with dream enactment and potential injury; a 2021 critical review describes clinical dream-enactment history plus video-polysomnographic confirmation as necessary for diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8739295/
- [statement] The AASM recommends a safe RBD sleeping environment: remove weapons and dangerous bedside objects, pad or move sharp furniture, place a soft surface beside the bed, and consider separate sleeping for severe uncontrolled behaviors. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] For secondary RBD, the AASM advises accounting for clonazepam-related sedation and imbalance, especially in older adults; reported adverse events include daytime sleepiness, dizziness and postural instability. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] The 2020 PD insomnia review places CBT-I within the general first-line approach to insomnia while emphasizing that PD-specific randomized trials were small; general insomnia evidence should not be presented as large-trial PD-specific proof. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated melatonin and eszopiclone for PD insomnia as possibly useful despite insufficient efficacy evidence; these ratings should not be rewritten as established efficacy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] NICE advises people with PD who have daytime sleepiness or sudden sleep onset not to drive and to consider occupational hazards; medication adjustment should follow specialist advice. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] Modafinil evidence in PD is mixed: MDS 2019 calls it possibly useful while retaining insufficient efficacy evidence, and one placebo-controlled trial found no significant improvement in either Epworth scores or objective sleep latency. Response should not be assumed. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1739456/
- [statement] For PD patients with obstructive sleep apnea, the 2019 MDS review considered CPAP likely efficacious and possibly useful for improving sleep and daytime sleepiness; this evidence does not apply indiscriminately to all PD sleepiness. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] The 2025 systematic review pooled pharmacological trials and reported improvements in insomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness but no statistically significant pooled RBD benefit; certainty ranged from very low to moderate. This class-level pooling does not establish efficacy of every included drug. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12706981/
- [statement] RBD involves loss of normal REM muscle atonia and dream enactment that can injure the patient or bed partner. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7027846/
- [statement] The cited sources note that clonazepam for RBD carries risks including morning sedation, gait imbalance or falls, cognitive adverse effects, and worsening sleep-disordered breathing; age and pre-existing imbalance affect selection and dosing. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] The 2023 AASM guideline conditionally supports transdermal rivastigmine for PD-associated RBD, based on one randomized trial; reported adverse effects include hypotension, asthenia, daytime sleepiness and nausea. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
